gotchas: Recorded so nobody researches it twice: this is NOT the 3U rack. It is 5U, has two RS-485 RJ45 ports rather than one, uses four DIP switches for a plain address rather than seven for baud-plus-protocol-menu, and has a separate Battery-COMM inter-pack port. None of the models on the Quebec retail list appear to be this

Schneider support is a firmware fork. The manual says to "update the battery with the Schneider firmware available from Volthium technical service" using an RS485-USB cable. The same physical pack runs different firmware for different inverters, so a bench reading proves nothing about another unit of the same SKU.

Address numbering is protocol-dependent, and the rules contradict each other across sections: Growatt wants the master at ID 2 and explicitly says "No battery has the #1 position, that's normal!"; Sol-Ark and Victron want the master at ID 1 and say to skip ID 2; Schneider wants ID 1 then consecutive. There is no single
Which physical port carries the daisy chain also changes per protocol: Growatt chains over the RS-485 ports, Sol-Ark/Victron/Schneider chain over the Battery-COMM ports.

The Victron VE.CAN cable is not straight-through. The manual gives battery side B-V, Green, B-Orange, Blue, B-Blue, Orange, B-Brown, Brown against Victron side B-Green, Green, Orange, B-Brown, B-Orange, Brown, Blue, B-Blue. The pack cannot be the terminated end.
unmappedReports: BMS-pushed bulk charge voltage (default 55.0 V) — no MetricKind. This is a limit the pack advertises to the charger, not a measurement., BMS-pushed float voltage (default 54 V) — no MetricKind., BMS-pushed charge current limit (50 A on 5 kW packs, 90 A on 10 kW) — set-charge-current-limit exists as a CommandKind, but there is no MetricKind for *reading back* the limit the BMS is asking for., BMS-pushed discharge current limit (100 A / 150 A) — no MetricKind and no CommandKind.
